key_insight: Weekly blood microsampling detected rising interferon gene signatures before and during dermatomyositis flares, suggesting a potential early molecular flare signal.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help clinicians anticipate flare risk earlier than symptom-driven visits alone and monitor disease activity more continuously.
method: 6 women with inactive/minimally active dermatomyositis were followed for 6 months
Participants self-reported weekly PtGA scores and self-collected weekly 125 uL blood microsamples
RNA sequencing and gene-set analyses were used to compare flare vs no-flare timepoints
evidence_signal: In 54 blood samples across 9 timepoints, interferon scores and IFN-related gene sets were higher in flare-associated and pre-flare samples than in no-flare samples.
watch_item: This was a very small feasibility study, so larger validation is needed before longitudinal IFN signatures can be used for routine flare prediction.
paper_title: Longitudinal interferon signatures are associated with disease flare in dermatomyositis
